workerProtocol._comment: epic-whp party-to-pipeline 自建雙向握手協議. resumeEnabled=true landed by whp-1-poc-resume-and-closeevent (2026-07-26, see SSoT §20.2.1 + docs/tracking/archived/epic-whp/whp-1-poc-resume-and-closeevent.track.md for evidence-grade caveats). 9 guardian*/stall*/ackCheckIntervalMin keys landed by whp-7-guardian-daemon (2026-07-28, see docs/implementation-artifacts/specs/epic-whp/whp-7-guardian-daemon-spec.md §4.4) -- guardianDispatchGraceSec + guardianScopeMaxFiles are NOT in original SSoT §22.8 list (added deliberately, see spec §4.4). dispatchConfirmSec + reaperOnDispatch landed by whp-4-write-path-wiring (2026-07-29, BR-130): dispatchConfirmSec=60 is the SSoT §22.8 authoritative value, superseding guardian-tick.js:51's internal fallback of 30 -- this is a deliberate, non-silent behavior change: the guardian's dispatching-ghost death threshold moves from 150s to 180s (dispatchConfirmSec + guardianDispatchGraceSec). autoCloseEnabled landed by whp-2-no-autoclose-liveness (2026-08-01, SSoT §22.8) -- CORRECTED at code-review (2026-08-01): this key currently has NO runtime consumer. Per BR-012 (user ruling: retired blocks are archived as comments, not flag-gated), the close-watchdog and dispatcher lingering-branch code paths were unconditionally commented out in all 4 worker-*.ps1 and dispatch-general.ps1, not wired behind this flag -- flipping it to true is a silent no-op today. It is kept as a documented placeholder for a future flag-gated re-enable (should one ever be built) and as an explicit signal that the retirement is intentional and named, not merely dropped. The REAL rollback path for this Story's change is `git revert` the whp-2 commit, or manually un-commenting the 5 blocks BR-012 preserved verbatim (see worker-lifecycle-judgment.md + party-to-pipeline-自建雙向協議-架構規格書.md 第十一章 for the archived originals + rationale). closeConfirmSec landed by whp-6-directive-delivery-and-close (2026-08-01, BR-032): bounded confirmation window (seconds) close-worker.ps1's C6 step polls for wrapper_pid death after taskkill -- absent/unreadable config falls back to the same default (15) hard-coded in close-worker-ops.js, per BR032_CloseConfirmSecFromConfig_DefaultsTo15WhenAbsent. guardianStaleMin/digestDetailCap/ackEscalateAfterRounds landed by whp-8-report-ack-notify (2026-08-02, BR-012/BR-029): the create-story SDD spec assumed ackEscalateAfterRounds pre-existed (whp-7's own spec text 'Left to whp-8' was misread as 'already added') -- a repo-wide grep at dev-story time confirmed zero occurrences and guardian-tick.js has never read any such threshold, so this is a genuine new addition, not a read of a pre-existing value; guardian-tick.test.js's AC12 lock (which asserted this key's ABSENCE, comment 'whp-8 owns it') was updated in the same commit. Left to owning story: reviewReminderMin (whp-10). hookGraceSec landed by whp-11-d2-inline-revise (2026-08-02, BR-004/025/026): bounded-wait ceiling (seconds) stop-report.ps1's D2 branch polls for a pending controller-to-worker directive before writing reported -- absent config falls back to 120 (in-code default), out-of-range values clamp to [0,300] and log D2-GRACE-CLAMPED (deliberately narrower than this file's own phaseTimeouts, which run into the millions of ms -- BR-026 chose to clamp rather than trust an arbitrarily large configured value, since the wait blocks the Stop hook chain's remaining 9 hooks if they run sequentially, see dev_notes 「Stop chain 排序與 timeout」). 0 is a valid, deliberate value -- see AC12: it fully disables the poll (single check, zero wait), the documented zero-cost opt-out. knockEnabled landed by whp-12-knock-console-inject (2026-08-02, BR-022): kill switch for the slow-loop knock (console input injection into an already-idle worker). UNLIKE autoCloseEnabled above, this key HAS a real runtime consumer -- knock-worker-ops.js resolveKnockEnabled() reads it on every decideKnock() call and returns reason='disabled' with zero DB reads and zero injection when false; smoke Group 16 asserts both the grep-able consumer and the actual no-op behaviour (AC10 was written specifically to keep this key from becoming a second autoCloseEnabled). Absent/unreadable config defaults to true: the PoC verdict is viable (P1 + P2a 3/3, see Story dev_notes), so a missing config must not silently disable an already-validated channel.
